ir.name: rank_adjacent_positive_inverse_gap_pairs_weighted
ir.intuition: Select adjacent rank pairs where the winner's objective is strictly better (lower), weighting pairs by the inverse of the positive objective gap plus one. This emphasizes pairs that are close in objective value to provide a smoother weighting that avoids zero weights, increasing pair coverage for robust pairwise training.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N]
    rank = feature_cache['rank']  # [B, N]
    batch_size, n = objective.shape
    # Construct pairwise rank matrices
    rank_w = rank.unsqueeze(2)  # [B, N, 1]
    rank_l = rank.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1, N]
    # Winner rank exactly one better (lower) than loser
    is_adjacent = (rank_l - rank_w) == 1
    # Objective gap: winner objective - loser objective
    gap = objective.unsqueeze(2) - objective.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, N, N]
    # positive gap mask (winner better than loser considering lower_is_better)
    positive_gap_mask = gap < 0
    valid_mask = is_adjacent & positive_gap_mask
    b_idx, w_idx, l_idx = valid_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    if b_idx.numel() == 0:
        # Return empty PrefBatch with proper types
        return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx.to(torch.int64), w_idx.to(torch.int64), l_idx.to(torch.int64)), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'rank_adjacent_positive_inverse_gap_pairs_weighted'})
    # Compute positive gaps as positive values
    pos_gap_vals = (-gap[b_idx, w_idx, l_idx])  # positive values
    # weight: inverse gap plus one to avoid zero division, smooth weighting
    weight = 1.0 / (pos_gap_vals + 1.0)
    max_pairs = extra.get('pairing_budget', 16)
    n_pairs = weight.size(0)
    if n_pairs > max_pairs:
        weight_sorted, top_idx = weight.topk(max_pairs, largest=True, sorted=False)
        b_idx = b_idx[top_idx]
        w_idx = w_idx[top_idx]
        l_idx = l_idx[top_idx]
        weight = weight_sorted
    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx.to(torch.int64), w_idx.to(torch.int64), l_idx.to(torch.int64)),
        weight=weight,
        meta={'builder': 'rank_adjacent_positive_inverse_gap_pairs_weighted'}
    )

ir.name: weighted_advantage_exp_margin_logsigmoid_scaled_weighted_mean_loss_v4
ir.intuition: Replaced the linear scaling of (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) by normalizing advantage_gap with an exponential margin term to reduce similarity to prior losses. The margin is now computed as exp(clamped mean advantage) minus 1, giving a smooth, nonlinear adaptive margin. This avoids direct shift subtraction and linearly scaled inputs, introducing a structurally different transformation that still respects pairwise margin and debias properties while preserving weighted mean aggregation. This structural shift improves novelty and numeric stability.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon=1e-6
mean_adv = mean(advantage_gap)
margin = exp(clamp(abs(mean_adv), 0, 1)) - 1
norm = max(mean(norm(advantage_gap)), epsilon)
x_raw = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm
x = margin * x_raw
x = clamp(x, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(x)
loss_weighted = loss * weight
return sum(loss_weighted) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    epsilon = 1e-6
    mean_adv = ops.mean(advantage_gap)
    margin = ops.sub(ops.exp(ops.clamp(ops.abs(mean_adv), 0.0, 1.0)), 1.0)
    norm_per_sample = ops.norm(advantage_gap)
    norm = ops.maximum(ops.mean(norm_per_sample), epsilon)
    x_raw = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm)
    x = ops.mul(margin, x_raw)
    x = ops.clamp(x, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
    loss_weighted = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_mean = ops.div(ops.sum(loss_weighted), ops.maximum(ops.sum(weight), epsilon))
    return loss_mean
